title: Runtime ↔ Control Plane migration checklist and compatibility guidelines
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working checklist and compatibility guide for migrating customer private deployments where the runtime and control plane are being upgraded independently (split upgrade). It focuses on minimizing client API breaks, preserving cached KV/state, and enabling safe rollbacks.

Scope:
- Applies to Private (VPC/on-prem) installs running: kubernetes-based runtime (k8s 1.24-1.26), control plane components (helm charts), and Terraform-based infra provisioning.
- Includes: API compatibility guarantees, terraform module change handling, canary upgrade pattern, verification tests, rollback recipes.
- Excludes: full on-prem bare-metal OCI builds (separate playbook).

High-level goals:
1) No downtime for existing API clients during 90% of upgrades.
2) Fast rollback path (<30 minutes end-to-end) for a canary failure.
3) Clear compatibility matrix for control plane <-> runtime <-> client SDKs.

Pre-upgrade checklist (local / customer):
- Inventory: record runtime version, control plane version, model bundles, quantization profile, and Kubernetes node types. (TODO: export script: ./tools/export-deploy-metadata.sh)
- Backups: snapshot DB and object store metadata (etcd/pg) and export Redis/KV snapshot.
- Terraform: run `terraform plan` and `terraform state pull` into a local file, ensure provider versions pinned (hashicorp/kubernetes provider >= 2.8).
- Throttle: verify rate limits and autoscaling policies are set so canary traffic won't be throttled in unexpected ways.

Compatibility matrix (example):
- Control Plane 1.8.x ⇄ Runtime 2.2.x: supported (compat shim available).
- Control Plane 1.9.x ⇄ Runtime 2.3.x: recommended for new installs.
- Client SDKs older than v0.14: may require API shim for new /v2/ headers — see API compatibility section.

API compatibility guidelines:
- Maintain stable /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings endpoints for minimum one minor control plane release after introducing /v2.
- Add feature flags in control plane to turn on new behaviors (structured output enforcement, tool-calling) per-route. Use `featureFlag:runtime_compat_mode` until clients upgraded.
- For breaking changes: provide runtime-side shim mapping (header translation + response shape rewriter) deployed on ingress until client upgrade adoption > 80%.

Terraform module migration notes:
- Don't rename resource addresses in state; prefer to add new module and phasing plan:
  1) Create new module `private_runtime_v2` with updated variables but referencing the same provider and avoid changing resource IDs.
  2) Use `terraform state mv` to move any resources intentionally only when doing final cutover. Example: `terraform state mv module.runtime.null_resource.runtime-bootstrap module.runtime_v2.null_resource.bootstrap`
- State locking: ensure S3 backend + DynamoDB lock or equivalent before any plan/apply.
- Provider pinning: lock k8s provider and helm provider to known-working versions. Record in `versions.tf` and commit.
- Migration tip: split infra change into two applies — infra-only (new k8s node pool / taints) and control-plane deployment (helm upgrade).

Canary and rollout strategy:
1) Canary cluster or subset of nodes: label nodes `upgrade-canary=true` and schedule a small replica set of runtime pods there.
2) Route 1–2% of tenant traffic (or 5–10 requests per minute) to canary via smart routing (console rollout policy).
3) Run smoke tests: token-cost sanity, simple generation prompt, embedding consistency, latency p95.
4) Monitor for 30 minutes for errors and latency regressions. Metrics to watch: 5xx rate, inference-runtime-retry, token-cost-per-request, kv-cache-hit-rate, model-eviction-count.
5) If stable, increment traffic by doubling every 30–60 minutes until 100%.

Validation test-suite (must pass on canary):
- End-to-end generation test with seeded prompts and checksum of top-1 tokens.
- Embedding cosine-sanity test against baseline vectors.
- KV cache warmup and eviction test: verify key persistence across restart when expected.
- Backpressure & batching behavior check under synthetic QPS.

Rollback recipes (fastest path):
- Control plane rollback (no infra change): use helm rollback to prior release (helm rollback redwood-controlplane <revision>) and flip routing policy back to previous model variant.
- Runtime rollback: scale up previous runtime ReplicaSet and scale down new one; use label-based routing to send traffic back. If runtime artifacts are harmful (model format incompatible), immediately mount prior model cache from snapshot.
- Terraform/state rollback: do not attempt to revert state to prior versions in place. Instead, restore state from a known-good state file copied before the migration and run a targeted apply into a staging account to validate first.

Known risk areas & mitigations:
- KV cache format change: always ship a migration layer that treats unknown keys as miss (lazy migrate). Provide `--preserve-old-keys` option during rollout for 24–48 hours.
- API semantic drift: maintain contract tests against upstream client SDKs; failing tests trigger immediate canary halt.
- DB schema incompatible migrations: prefer expand-then-contract pattern and multi-version support in code.

Operational runbook (on-call steps):
1) If canary error rate > 1% absolute or latency p95 degrade > 200ms: pause rollout and reduce traffic to 0% for canary.
2) Collect logs: `kubectl logs -l app=runtime -n redwood --since=15m` and core dumps.
3) If rollout pause doesn't stabilize in 10 minutes: execute rollback recipe.
4) Notify stakeholders: #private-deploys Slack, then page eng-sre and eng-private-deployments leads.

Open TODOs / questions:
- Should we enforce model bundle signature verification at ingest to avoid incompatible models during runtime upgrade? (Marcus to research)
- Add automated `terraform state` sanity check in CI (Ben to prototype).
- Document migration windows expectation for customers (Lina to draft customer-comms).

Appendix: quick commands
- Snapshot PG: `pg_dump -Fc -f backup-$(date +%F).dump`
- Terraform state pull: `terraform state pull > pre-upgrade-state.json`
- Helm dry-run: `helm upgrade --install redwood-controlplane ./charts/controlplane --namespace redwood --dry-run`
- Promote rollback: `helm rollback redwood-controlplane 3`

Notes to self: keep this doc lean, move finalized procedures into Confluence after first successful customer rollout.
